The best cold email marketing agencies in 2026 are ManasFlow for teams that want an outbound system built in their own accounts, Belkins for enterprise appointment setting, Martal Group for SaaS sellers, and CIENCE for published, performance-linked pricing. The biggest difference between them is who owns the domains, inboxes and data when the contract ends.

Cold email still works for B2B, but the mechanics have changed. Inbox providers tightened bulk-sender rules in 2024, so deliverability now depends on separate sending domains, warmed inboxes, low volume per inbox, and lists that are verified before anything sends. An agency that gets those basics wrong burns your domain. One that gets them right gives you a pipeline channel you can scale.

This guide compares 8 cold email agencies on services, pricing, infrastructure ownership, and independent reviews. Every price and review count below was checked on the agency's own site or its Clutch profile on October 21, 2026.

Disclosure: ManasFlow wrote this guide and ranks itself first. We rank ourselves first for one reason: we build the whole outbound system (Clay enrichment, Instantly and HeyReach sequences, CRM sync, and the automation between them) in your accounts, and we can run it or hand it over. We build automation; we do not staff an appointment-setting team. If you want a large SDR team calling and emailing for you against a meeting target, Belkins, Martal Group or LevelUp Leads will fit better.
Best cold email agencies: a brief overview
ManasFlow: Best overall for automation-first teams: we build and run the Instantly, HeyReach and Clay system in your accounts, wired into your CRM.
Belkins: Best for enterprise and mid-market appointment setting across every channel.

CIENCE: Best for published per-SDR pricing with part of the fee tied to meetings held.
Leadium: Best for email, LinkedIn and calls on month-to-month contracts.
LevelUp Leads: Best for phone-heavy, high-volume SDR pods with email in the mix.
Cleverly: Best for small budgets and LinkedIn-first outreach.

1. ManasFlow, best overall cold email agency for automation-first teams

ManasFlow approaches cold email as an outbound automation problem. We build and run the system: Clay or Apollo for list building and enrichment, verification before anything sends, Instantly for email sequences and HeyReach for LinkedIn, with replies, meetings and opt-outs synced back into your CRM. Our own outbound runs on Instantly, HeyReach, Attio, Unipile and n8n, so we hand over the same kind of system we operate.

The difference from a classic appointment-setting shop is ownership. Domains, inboxes, sequences and tables sit in your accounts, documented, so the channel keeps working if you bring it in-house later. Our cold email agency service covers the build, the copy and the monitoring. A common build is a signal-based outbound workflow, where a trigger such as a job change or hiring post becomes the opening line of the email.

2. Belkins, best for enterprise appointment setting

Belkins runs omnichannel appointment setting: cold email, cold and intent-based calling, voicemail, SMS and WhatsApp, LinkedIn and paid ads. Its own copywriters write the sequences, and its email specialists set up the domains, warm the mailboxes and monitor sender reputation. It also offers outsourced SDRs, deliverability consulting and ABM.
Belkins has the largest review base in this list, with 234 Clutch reviews at 4.9. Plans are monthly retainers set by annual appointment targets, from 100+ appointments a year on the Growth plan.
Main features
Omnichannel outreach toward an annual appointment target
In-house copywriting and deliverability team
Outsourced SDRs and ABM programs
Best for
Mid-market and enterprise companies with a defined meeting target and budget
Pricing
Custom quote; Growth plan targets 100+ appointments per year, Growth Plus 200+

Cons

3. Martal Group, best for B2B SaaS and tech companies

Martal Group provides outsourced sales executives who run cold email, LinkedIn follow-ups and power-dialer calls. Each executive gets a custom sending domain managed by Martal's deliverability team. Copy is drafted with its AI tool and edited by staff. Its focus industries are B2B SaaS, IT, fintech, HR tech, insurtech and cleantech.
Higher tiers add discovery calls and closing support, paid as a flat fee plus commission. Martal has 109 Clutch reviews at 4.8.
Main features
Outsourced SDRs running email, LinkedIn and calls
Managed sending domains per executive
Optional discovery and closing support

SaaS and tech sellers that want demos booked and some pipeline work done by the same team

4. CIENCE, best for published, performance-linked pricing

CIENCE staffs SDR teams that run cold calls, email and LinkedIn on its graph8 platform. Its site says AI drafts the opener and the SDR reviews it, calls and handles the reply. It is the only agency in this list that publishes full prices.

Pricing is a campaign team at $2,000 a month, the graph8 platform at $499 a month, and SDRs from $1,750 per month offshore or $3,500 in the US and Europe. A bonus tied to held meetings applies on top, starting at 60% of target. Contracts are month-to-month.

Pricing starts at $5,000 a month, prepaid, with a three-month initial commitment. LevelUp has 61 Clutch reviews at 5.0.

How we ranked these cold email agencies

We started from the agencies that rank for "cold email agency" searches and the ones repeatedly named in buyer threads, then checked each site and Clutch profile on October 21, 2026. We excluded firms whose services had changed away from cold email and firms with very poor public reviews. The ranking weighs four things: who owns the sending infrastructure, how clearly each firm fits a buyer type, pricing transparency, and independent review evidence. ManasFlow is first on ownership and system scope. On review volume it trails the established firms, which we list as a con.
How to choose the best cold email agency
Which cold email agency fits your situation
1) Rent a channel or build one?

Staffed agencies rent you a channel: their people, their domains, their process. Builders set up the channel in your accounts and either run it or hand it over. Renting is faster to start. Building keeps the asset.
If you want to rent: Belkins, Martal Group, LevelUp Leads or CIENCE
If you want to own: ManasFlow or Growth Rhino
2) Who owns the domains, inboxes and lists?

Ask this in the first call and get the answer in the contract. If the agency owns the domains, your sender reputation leaves with them. If the lists live in their database, you start from zero when you switch.
Assets in your name by default: ManasFlow, Growth Rhino
